purpose: Minimal optional Blender-authored investigations for Engineering Fieldnotes. Only ship 3D that supports spatial discovery or user-controlled counterfactual inspection beyond replaying a video.
ownership: Authors own only their assigned concepts in those three paths. Coordinator owns public/spatial/shared, viewer.html, shared build and page integration.

scene_json.title: Short title
scene_json.description: One sentence explaining what to investigate
scene_json.initialCaption: One short invitation to look or change something.
scene_json.interactionHint: Drag to look around · scroll to zoom
scene_json.fallback: One or two sentences explaining the observed relationship without WebGL.

module: interaction.js exports default function setup(ctx) returning {update(dt, elapsed), reset(), dispose()}. update returns true while animation needs another frame, false when idle. Do not start your own RAF. No imports needed; THREE is supplied.

ctx.model: Loaded glTF root; exported Blender Z-up becomes Three Y-up. getObjectByName uses glTF names (spaces may become underscores).
ctx.caption(text): Set the sole visible explanatory sentence; keep concise and factual.
ctx.addAction(label,fn): Adds a button, max TWO; returns button for label/disabled updates. A reset button is supplied by host. Every essential action must be keyboard reachable through these buttons, even when objects can be clicked.
ctx.onPick(fn): Register callback receiving zero or one nearest visible mesh intersection for click/tap, not drag. No picking through solid walls or hidden objects. Walk ancestors to identify the logical object.
ctx.invalidate(): Request rendering/animation after a state change.
ctx.view(position,target): Change camera and orbit target using arrays in Three coordinates, then invalidate.
ctx.reducedMotion: Boolean. Respect it: static state changes instead of long flythroughs.

constraints: One scene; at most two primary controls plus Reset; no sidebars, quizzes, staged forms, dashboards, onboarding, text walls or floating text cards. Labels may clarify an object but are not the explanatory mechanism.

Default scene is still. No motion before explicit interaction. Interaction can be a section cut, changing a boundary, inspecting hidden route, comparing local perspectives, revealing competing effects, etc. Generic moving balls between labeled boxes is insufficient.

Warm ivory material, charcoal details, one restrained amber accent, legible geometry at a 420px wide panel. Browser host provides lights and a warm background; include any essential plinth in your asset. Blender asset must include physical, crafted geometry; do not just create cubes and labels.

Keep asset origin near zero and dimensions roughly within 12 units, camera sensible. No exported lights/cameras/ground unless essential to concept. Physical illustrations are metaphors, not claims of measured model behavior.
Provide source and execute Blender (installed /opt/homebrew/bin/blender) with --threads 2. Retain .blend and export GLB; render one poster. No movies or huge texture assets.

Write intent.json with concept, mechanism, spatialBenefit, beyondVideoTest, interaction, expectedObservations, sourceGuide, limitations, authorModel. Set authorModel anthropic/claude-opus-5-5. Do not self-approve; Astra critique follows.

If a concept has no honest spatial benefit, make a concrete attempt and explain evidence in intent.json; mark candidate unsuitable rather than dressing a diagram in 3D. Coordinator will review and decide retry/omit.

Run module syntax check, inspect Blender output, verify required node names and initial camera bounds. Coordinator handles integrated browser QA; do not manipulate the shared browser viewport or others tabs. Standalone preview URL /spatial/viewer.html?concept=<id>.
